historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission decided to build an enclosed swimming pool at Garfield Square instead of at the Mission Playground, moving the bond money and the architect William Gladstone Merchant's contract to the new site.

With the 1947 bond fund nearly spent and the bids 35 percent above Hamilton's two years earlier, the Recreation and Park Commission awarded a contract for the Garfield Square swimming pool alone, without the planned building, to Cahill Construction Co. at $425,000.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved in principle a plan for new facilities at Garfield Square, drawn up for the East Mission Council with the Community Design Center by the architect Harry Glasscock, though no city money was available for it.
